Mina Patel: Quick heads-up — ran perf smoke on the fp8+int4 hybrid path on H100, continuous_batcher enabled. Seeing p99 token latency regress ~18% on len=512 compared to int8 baseline. Attaching short trace.

Ravi Chen: Can you paste the run config & top-level numbers?

Mina Patel: Config: `continuous_batcher.enabled=true, max_batch_tokens=65536, pad_to=uniform, pad_align=64, quant_profile=hybrid-fp8-int4`
Raw: `throughput=11.2k tok/s -> 10.3k tok/s (-8%), p50=12ms, p95=48ms, p99=78ms (was 66ms)`

Mina Patel: Trace snippet shows kernel selector switching to `fp8_matmul_fallback` for certain shapes. Also see lots of small memcpy ops when kv-cache split happens.

Lina Gomez: H100 only? A100 runs differently because of mem bandwidth.

Mina Patel: repro on H100 only so far. Re-ran with `REDWOOD_TRACE=kernel_selector,kvcache` and this popped up: 
```
[selector] chosen_kernel=fp8_matmul_fallback cost=1234 fallback_reason=shape_align_mismatch
[kv] split_count=3 memcpy_bytes=12.7MB memcpy_ops=48
```

Ravi Chen: My guess: calibration scales for fp8 packing changed the cost model ordering. If selector overestimates fp8 per-op speed for those shapes, it will pick it even with high memcpy overhead. Can you try forcing `int8_gemm_v2` env override?

Mina Patel: did `REDWOOD_FORCE_KERNEL=int8_gemm_v2` — p99 returned to ~67ms, throughput 10.7k tok/s, but p50 improved slightly. Short sequences (<=64) throughput regressed ~9% vs pure int8.

Anya Satterfield: Sounds like padding waste + pack alignment interplay. continuous_batcher pads microbatches to align to 64, fp8 packer needs 32-alignment internally, causing extra tile work. Proposal: add a cheap heuristic: if pad_waste_ratio > 0.25 AND median_seq < 128 then prefer int8 path or lower batcher pad_align.

Ravi Chen: Agreed. Also add a metric to the kernel selector: estimate_extra_memcpy_cycles = memcpy_bytes / mem_bw_estimate and factor into cost. That would demote kernels that incur many splits.
